paras.text: 2. Keeping the budget secret (Secret) or open (Open)
paras.urdu: 2۔ بجٹ چھپانا (Secret) یا ظاہر (Open) کرنا:
paras.pashto: 2. د بودجې پټول (Secret) یا ښکاره (Open) کول

paras.text: Individuals usually keep the account of their income and expenditure hidden and do not like to disclose their budget, because in it there are many social and psychological expediencies, e.g. if the income of some person is less than his expenditure, then if it is disclosed to his relatives, the illusion of his white-collar respectability is broken; if the income of some individual is very much, then too he does not disclose it for fear of income tax or the fear of thieves and robbers. But the case of the government is the reverse: instead of hiding its budget, it publicises it, and by presenting it in parliament tells the public from where, how much income will be obtained and on which heads it will be spent.
paras.urdu: عام افراد اپنی آمدنی و خرچ کا حساب عموماً پوشیدہ رکھتے ہیں اور اپنے بجٹ کو ظاہر کرنا پسند نہیں کرتے، کیونکہ اس میں کئی سماجی اور نفسیاتی مصلحتیں ہوتی ہیں۔ مثلاً اگر کسی شخص کی آمدنی اس کے خرچ سے کم ہو تو اس کے عزیز و اقارب پر اس کی سفید پوشی کا بھرم کھل جاتا ہے، اگر کسی فرد کی آمدنی بہت زیادہ ہو تو وہ بھی انکم ٹیکس کے خوف یا چور اچکے کے ڈر سے اسے ظاہر نہیں کرتا۔ لیکن حکومت کا معاملہ الٹ ہے، وہ اپنا بجٹ چھپانے کی بجائے مشتہر کرتی ہے۔ اور اسے پارلیمنٹ میں پیش کر کے عوام کو بتاتی ہے کہ اسے کہاں کہاں سے، کتنی کتنی آمدنی حاصل ہوگی اور وہ کس کس مد پر خرچ کی جائے گی۔

paras.text: By this is meant such income or receipt which is obtained from different kinds of taxes, e.g. (i) direct tax (Direct Tax), (ii) indirect tax (Indirect Tax).

Sources of income of the government (Sources of Income)

The governments of the modern age obtain finance and income for performing their defence, social, economic, developmental and other functions, of which there are the following two sources:

1. Tax revenue

By this is meant such income or receipt which is obtained from different kinds of taxes, e.g. (i) direct tax (Direct Tax), (ii) indirect tax (Indirect Tax).

A direct tax means such a tax whose burden too falls on the person on whom it is imposed, e.g. income tax (Income Tax), or wealth tax (Wealth Tax), or gift (Gift) tax and property tax (Property Tax) etc. These taxes are imposed on the income, wealth or property of people; therefore they themselves pay them and bear their burden. In contrast, an indirect tax means such a tax which the individual or company on whom it is imposed pays itself, but, transferring it onwards, recovers from others, e.g. tax on imports and exports. This tax the importer or exporter pays, but includes the amount of the tax in the price of the thing being imported or exported and recovers it from customers. Likewise sales (Sales) (i.e. bikri) tax and excise duty etc. too are indirect taxes.

By this is meant such receipt which the government obtains in exchange for its production, business or some other services, e.g. the government collects price or fee by selling the produce of government forests or the manufactures of industrial institutions, or by providing communication services. In non-tax income those sums too are included which the government raises by taking loans inside or outside the country.

2. Keeping the budget secret (Secret) or open (Open)

Individuals usually keep the account of their income and expenditure hidden and do not like to disclose their budget, because in it there are many social and psychological expediencies, e.g. if the income of some person is less than his expenditure, then if it is disclosed to his relatives, the illusion of his white-collar respectability is broken; if the income of some individual is very much, then too he does not disclose it for fear of income tax or the fear of thieves and robbers. But the case of the government is the reverse: instead of hiding its budget, it publicises it, and by presenting it in parliament tells the public from where, how much income will be obtained and on which heads it will be spent.

Public revenue and tax culture (Public Revenue and Tax Culture)

The tax system which is established for the government, while adopting different methods and making laws in this sector for obtaining income through taxes, is called tax culture (mehsulati tamaddun).

Sources of income of the government (Sources of Income)

The governments of the modern age obtain finance and income for performing their defence, social, economic, developmental and other functions, of which there are the following two sources:

1. Tax revenue

By this is meant such income or receipt which is obtained from different kinds of taxes, e.g. (i) direct tax (Direct Tax), (ii) indirect tax (Indirect Tax).

A direct tax means such a tax whose burden too falls on the person on whom it is imposed, e.g. income tax (Income Tax), or wealth tax (Wealth Tax), or gift (Gift) tax and property tax (Property Tax) etc. These taxes are imposed on the income, wealth or property of people; therefore they themselves pay them and bear their burden. In contrast, an indirect tax means such a tax which the individual or company on whom it is imposed pays itself, but, transferring it onwards, recovers from others, e.g. tax on imports and exports. This tax the importer or exporter pays, but includes the amount of the tax in the price of the thing being imported or exported and recovers it from customers. Likewise sales (Sales) (i.e. bikri) tax and excise duty etc. too are indirect taxes.

2. Non-tax income (Non-Tax Revenue)

By this is meant such receipt which the government obtains in exchange for its production, business or some other services, e.g. the government collects price or fee by selling the produce of government forests or the manufactures of industrial institutions, or by providing communication services. In non-tax income those sums too are included which the government raises by taking loans inside or outside the country.

Here we state the detail of these different kinds of sources:

Tax (Tax) or levy

The most important source of government income is the tax. By it is meant such a payable sum on the citizens which they give to the government from their wealth or income … (continued on p.65)

براہِ راست ٹیکس سے مراد ایسا ٹیکس ہے جو جس شخص پر عائد کیا جائے اس کا بوجھ بھی اس پر پڑے، مثلاً انکم ٹیکس (Income Tax) یا دولت ٹیکس (Wealth Tax) یا ہبہ (Gift) ٹیکس اور پراپرٹی ٹیکس (Property Tax) وغیرہ۔ یہ ٹیکس لوگوں کی اپنی آمدنی یا دولت یا جائیداد پر عائد کیے جاتے ہیں اس لیے وہ خود ادا کرتے اور ان کا بوجھ اٹھاتے ہیں۔ ان کے برعکس بالواسطہ ٹیکس سے مراد ایسا ٹیکس ہے جو جس فرد یا کمپنی پر عائد کیا جائے وہ ادا تو خود کرے لیکن آگے منتقل کر کے دوسروں سے وصول کرے، مثلاً درآمدات و برآمدات پر ٹیکس۔ یہ ٹیکس امپورٹر یا ایکسپورٹر ادا کرتے ہیں لیکن ٹیکس کی رقم درآمد یا برآمد کی جانے والی شے کی قیمت میں شامل کر کے گاہکوں سے وصول کر لیتے ہیں۔ اسی طرح سیلز (Sales) (یعنی بکری) ٹیکس اور ایکسائز ڈیوٹی وغیرہ بھی بالواسطہ ٹیکس ہیں۔

2۔ غیر محصولاتی آمدنی (Non-Tax Revenue):

اس سے مراد ایسی وصولی ہے جو حکومت کو اپنی پیداوار، کاروبار یا بعض دیگر خدمات کے عوض حاصل ہوتی ہے، مثلاً حکومت سرکاری جنگلات کی پیداوار یا صنعتی اداروں کی مصنوعات فروخت کر کے یا مواصلاتی خدمات مہیا کر کے قیمت یا فیس وصول کرتی ہے۔ غیر محصولاتی آمدنی میں وہ رقوم بھی شامل ہیں جو حکومت ملک کے اندر یا باہر سے قرضہ لے کر فراہم کرتی ہے۔

ہم یہاں ان مختلف قسم کے ذرائع کی تفصیل بیان کرتے ہیں:

ٹیکس (Tax) یا محصول:

سرکاری آمدنی کا سب سے اہم ذریعہ ٹیکس ہوتا ہے۔ اس سے مراد شہریوں کے ذمے ایسی واجب الادا رقم ہے جو وہ اپنی دولت یا آمدنی … (ص 65 پر جاری)

i. Its payment is compulsory, i.e. the one on whom the tax is imposed — as it were, whose income is taxable — has to pay it compulsorily.

ii. The tax is obtained for the general collective purposes of the government; in exchange for it no direct benefit is given to the payer, i.e. whoever pays income tax cannot demand from the government that it should give him, in exchange for it, just as much benefit for his own person; rather the amount of the tax is spent for the collective and common (Collective) benefit of the nation.

The “non-tax income” of the government is as follows:

1. Fee (Fee)

By this is meant that sum which people pay in exchange for obtaining some service from the government, e.g. licence fee or tuition fee (Tution Fee). In Pakistan a fee is paid for making a licence for weapons, making a passport, playing hunting, or putting tickets on court papers.

2. Price of a thing or service (Price of Goods or Services)

By this is meant that income which the government obtains in exchange for selling its goods or services (Goods & Services), e.g. the sum which it obtains from petroleum, natural gas and the wood of forests etc. is counted under this head. The difference between fee and price is that the fee can be less or more than the cost of that service which the government provides to the public, but the price is equal to the service provided. The difference between tax and “price” is that the tax has to be given by every person on whom the rules apply, but the price has to be given only by him who buys some service or thing from the government.

3. State property (State Property)

The government also obtains income from government property, e.g. by selling government lands, or by taking out minerals from mines (Mines), or by selling the wood and other produce of forests. The Government of Pakistan obtains income by selling the salt coming out of mines, and by giving other mines on contract obtains income in the form of royalty (Royalty). Likewise it obtains income by selling the wood of forests from Hazara district, Dir, Chitral and the northern areas.

4. Productive works of the government (Productive Enterprises)

The government does some commercial business from which it obtains income in the form of profit, e.g. the income obtained from the departments of railway, post, telegraph, telephone and electricity etc.

حکومت ته له دولتي ملکیت هم عاید ترلاسه کېږي؛ لکه د دولتي ځمکو په پلورلو، یا له کانونو (Mines) د کاني توکو په ایستلو، یا د ځنګلونو د لرګیو او نورو تولیداتو په پلورلو. د پاکستان حکومت له کانونو د راوتونکې مالګې په پلورلو او نورو کانونو په ټیکه ورکولو د رایلټۍ (Royalty) په بڼه عاید ترلاسه کوي. همداسې د هزارې ولسوالۍ، دیر، چترال او شمالي سیمو د ځنګلونو د لرګیو په پلورلو عاید ترلاسه کوي.

4. د حکومت تولیدي کارونه (Productive Enterprises)

حکومت ځینې نور سوداګریز کاروبارونه کوي چې له هغو د ګټې په بڼه عاید ترلاسه کوي؛ لکه د رېل، پوسټ، ټیلګراف، ټیلیفون، برېښنا او نورو څانګو څخه ترلاسه شوی عاید.

د مالیو د لګولو اصول (Canons of Taxation)

حکومت (یعنې د یوه هېواد مالیې وزیر) باید د مالیو د پلي کولو پر وخت لاندې اصول په پام کې ونیسي، چې لومړي څلور یې پروفېسر اډم سمېت وړاندې کړي دي.

1. د مساوات اصل (Canon of Equity)

پروفېسر اډم سمېت لیکي چې د هر هېواد اوسېدونکي باید د خپل حکومت د ټینګښت لپاره د خپلې وړتیا سره سم برخه واخلي. دې ته د مساوات یا عدل اصل ویل کېږي. له دې مراد دا نه دی چې هر کس په برابر مقدار مالیه ورکړي، او نه یې مطلب دا دی چې هر سړی … (په ۶۶ مخ دوام لري)

(continued from p.64) … give to the government, so that it can meet those expenses which it has to bear for the collective benefit of the public. There are two characteristics of a tax:

i. Its payment is compulsory, i.e. the one on whom the tax is imposed — as it were, whose income is taxable — has to pay it compulsorily.

ii. The tax is obtained for the general collective purposes of the government; in exchange for it no direct benefit is given to the payer, i.e. whoever pays income tax cannot demand from the government that it should give him, in exchange for it, just as much benefit for his own person; rather the amount of the tax is spent for the collective and common (Collective) benefit of the nation.

The “non-tax income” of the government is as follows:

1. Fee (Fee)

By this is meant that sum which people pay in exchange for obtaining some service from the government, e.g. licence fee or tuition fee (Tution Fee). In Pakistan a fee is paid for making a licence for weapons, making a passport, playing hunting, or putting tickets on court papers.

2. Price of a thing or service (Price of Goods or Services)

By this is meant that income which the government obtains in exchange for selling its goods or services (Goods & Services), e.g. the sum which it obtains from petroleum, natural gas and the wood of forests etc. is counted under this head. The difference between fee and price is that the fee can be less or more than the cost of that service which the government provides to the public, but the price is equal to the service provided. The difference between tax and “price” is that the tax has to be given by every person on whom the rules apply, but the price has to be given only by him who buys some service or thing from the government.

3. State property (State Property)

The government also obtains income from government property, e.g. by selling government lands, or by taking out minerals from mines (Mines), or by selling the wood and other produce of forests. The Government of Pakistan obtains income by selling the salt coming out of mines, and by giving other mines on contract obtains income in the form of royalty (Royalty). Likewise it obtains income by selling the wood of forests from Hazara district, Dir, Chitral and the northern areas.

4. Productive works of the government (Productive Enterprises)

The government does some commercial business from which it obtains income in the form of profit, e.g. the income obtained from the departments of railway, post, telegraph, telephone and electricity etc.

Principles of imposing taxes (Canons of Taxation)

The government (i.e. the finance minister of a country), while enforcing taxes, should keep in view the following principles, of which the first four principles were presented by Professor Adam Smith.

1. Canon of equality (Canon of Equity)

Professor Adam Smith writes that the residents of every country should take part, according to their ability, for the stability of their government. (ص 64 سے جاری) … میں سے حکومت کو دیتے ہیں، تاکہ وہ ان اخراجات کو پورا کر سکے جو اسے عوام کے اجتماعی فائدے کے لیے اٹھانے پڑتے ہیں، ٹیکس کی دو خصوصیات ہیں:

i) اس کی ادائیگی لازمی ہوتی ہے یعنی جس پر ٹیکس عائد ہوتا ہے، گویا جس کی آمدنی قابلِ ٹیکس ہوتی ہے، سے یہ ضروری دینا پڑتا ہے۔

ii) ٹیکس حکومت کے عام اجتماعی مقاصد کے لیے حاصل کیا جاتا ہے، اس کے بدلے میں ٹیکس دینے والے کو براہِ راست کوئی فائدہ نہیں پہنچایا جاتا۔ یعنی جو شخص انکم ٹیکس ادا کرتا ہے، وہ اس کے بدلے میں اپنی ذات کے لیے اتنا ہی فائدہ اٹھانے کے لیے حکومت سے تقاضا نہیں کر سکتا، بلکہ ٹیکس کی رقم قوم کے اجتماعی اور مشترکہ (Collective) فائدہ کے لیے خرچ ہوتی ہے۔

حکومت کے ”غیر محصولاتی آمدنی“ درج ذیل ہیں:

1۔ فیس (Fee):

اس سے مراد وہ رقم ہے جو لوگ حکومت سے کوئی خدمت حاصل کرنے کے عوض ادا کرتے ہیں، مثلاً لائسنس فیس یا تعلیمی فیس (Tution Fee)۔ پاکستان میں اسلحہ کا لائسنس بنانے، پاسپورٹ بنوانے، شکار کھیلنے یا عدالتی کاغذات پر ٹکٹ لگانے کے لیے فیس ادا کی جاتی ہے۔

2۔ شے یا خدمت کی قیمت: (Price of Goods or Services)

اس سے مراد وہ آمدنی ہے جو حکومت کو اپنی اشیاء یا خدمات (Goods & Services) فروخت کرنے کے عوض حاصل ہوتی ہے، مثلاً پٹرولیم، قدرتی گیس اور جنگلات کی لکڑی وغیرہ سے جو رقم حاصل کرتی ہے وہ اس مد میں شمار ہوتی ہے۔ فیس اور قیمت میں یہ فرق ہے کہ فیس اس خدمت کی لاگت سے کم یا زیادہ ہو سکتی ہے۔ جو حکومت عوام کو مہیا کرتی ہے، لیکن قیمت مہیا کردہ خدمت کے برابر ہوتی ہے۔ ٹیکس اور ”قیمت“ میں یہ فرق ہے کہ ٹیکس ہر اس شخص کو دینا پڑتا ہے جس پر قواعد کے تحت لاگو ہو، لیکن قیمت صرف اسے ہی دینی پڑتی ہے جو حکومت سے کوئی خدمت یا شے خریدے۔

3۔ سرکاری جائیداد (State Property):

حکومت کو سرکاری جائیداد سے بھی آمدنی حاصل ہوتی ہے، مثلاً سرکاری زمینیں فروخت کر کے یا کانوں (Mines) سے معدنیات نکال کر یا جنگلات کی لکڑی اور دیگر پیداواریں فروخت کر کے۔ حکومت پاکستان کانوں سے نکلنے والے نمک کو فروخت کر کے اور دیگر کانیں ٹھیکہ پر دے کر رائلٹی (Royalty) کی شکل میں آمدنی حاصل کرتی ہے۔ اسی طرح ضلع ہزارہ، دیر، چترال اور شمالی علاقوں سے جنگلات کی لکڑی فروخت کر کے آمدنی حاصل کرتی ہے۔

4۔ حکومت کے پیداواری کام (Productive Enterprises):

حکومت بعض اور تجارتی کاروبار کرتی ہے جن سے اسے منافع کی صورت میں آمدنی حاصل ہوتی ہے، مثلاً ریل، ڈاک، تار، ٹیلیفون، بجلی وغیرہ کے محکموں سے حاصل ہونے والی آمدنی۔

ٹیکس عائد کرنے کے اصول (Canons of Taxation):

حکومت کو (یعنی کسی ملک کے وزیرِ مالیات کو) ٹیکس نافذ کرتے وقت، مندرجہ ذیل اصول پیشِ نظر رکھنے چاہئیں ان میں سے پہلے چار اصول پروفیسر آدم سمتھ نے پیش کیے ہیں۔

1۔ اصولِ مساوات (Canon of Equity):

پروفیسر آدم سمتھ لکھتے ہیں کہ ہر ملک کے باشندوں کو اپنی حکومت کے استحکام کے لیے، اپنی توفیق کے مطابق حصہ لینا چاہیے۔ اسے [مس]اوات یا عدل کا اصول کہا جاتا ہے، اس سے یہ مراد نہیں ہے کہ ہر شخص یکساں مقدار میں ٹیکس ادا کرے، نہ اس کا یہ مطلب ہے کہ ہر آدمی … (ص 66 پر جاری)
